Complaint Narrative
I, Sushila Devi Meena, resident of House No. 118, Ward 12, Hanuman Nagar, Chomu, state that my husband
Naresh Chand Meena worked as a property agent in the Chomu, Kaladera, and Sikar Road belt for about
twenty-two years. He ran a proprietary firm named Aravalli Bhoomi Associates from Shop 4, Hanuman Nagar
Market, and arranged the sale, resale, and part-payment booking of agricultural and converted land in the
villages around Chomu tehsil.
From about October 2025 my husband was working on land parcels described as Khasra No. 412/6 and
Khasra No. 418/2 of village Nangal Bharda, Tehsil Chomu, jointly with Kailash Narayan Sharma, a land
dealer of Vidhyadhar Nagar, and with a firm named Marudhar Estate Traders Pvt Ltd. He said buyers were
paying amounts between INR 6,00,000 and INR 47,00,000 each against agreements to sell and part-payment
receipts.
In February 2026 my husband became very disturbed. He told me that the jamabandi and mutation entries
shown to the buyers did not match the record he had himself seen at the patwar halka earlier, that mutation
entry No. 1179/2025-26 had been shown as sanctioned in favour of Marudhar Estate Traders Pvt Ltd on the

CASE-2026-JPR-HOM-527 | Fictional training-format case file | Not a record of any real event or person
Page 3
strength of a power-of-attorney which the recorded khatedar had never executed, and that the recorded
khatedar of Khasra No. 412/6 was an old man who had died some years earlier and whose heirs lived in
another district.
My husband told me in March 2026 that he had obtained a copy of the power-of-attorney bearing reference
DOC-CHM-2026-2184 and that the thumb impression and photograph on it were not of the person named in
it. He said the document had been used to transfer the land and re-sell it to buyers who paid through his own
office, and that the land was held in the name of the firm for other persons who had actually paid. He said he
had asked Kailash Narayan Sharma to return INR 92,00,000 passed on out of buyer payments, and had been
told to remain quiet and keep collecting instalments.
On 14 May 2026 two buyers, Om Prakash Yadav and Kamla Bai Jat, came to our house and demanded their
money back. My husband told them that he would return the amounts within one month and that he was going
to give a written complaint about the papers. That evening he told me that photocopies of the receipts, the
jamabandi extracts, the mutation order, and the power-of-attorney were kept in the office almirah and on his
computer.
On 21 May 2026 at about 20:15 hours my husband left the house on his motorcycle bearing registration
RJ-14-SM-2148, saying that Kailash Narayan Sharma had called him for a “final hisab” at the farmhouse near
the Kaladera bypass cut on Sikar Road and that he would return by 22:00 hours. He carried a green cloth file.
He did not return, and his mobile number +91-94140-52286 rang until about 21:10 hours and was thereafter
switched off.
At about 23:05 hours we were informed that a body was lying in the outbuilding of Shri Balaji Farmhouse. I
reached there with my brother and my son and identified the body of my husband. There were injuries on his
head and on the back of the neck. His mobile phone, the green cloth file, and his purse were not found with the
body. His motorcycle RJ-14-SM-2148 was standing near the outer gate.
I further state that in the fifteen days before his death my husband received repeated calls from
+91-99290-41628 and from +91-88900-63354 which he said were about the land money and the papers. On
19 May 2026 he showed me a message on his phone which said “akela aana, kagaz saath lana, hisab khatam.”
He also told me that a white vehicle bearing number RJ-14-CB-3092 had come twice to the office and that
persons in it had told him not to talk to the buyers.
I request lawful investigation into the death of my husband, into the forged jamabandi and mutation entries
relating to Khasra No. 412/6 and Khasra No. 418/2 of village Nangal Bharda, into the power-of-attorney
bearing reference DOC-CHM-2026-2184, into the persons for whose benami benefit the land and the money
were held, and into every person who caused, arranged, assisted, or benefited from his death.

Preliminary Observations
The case material indicates a land-transfer chain in which a power-of-attorney and a mutation entry appear
in favour of a firm, while the earlier revenue record shows a different recorded khatedar who is reported to
have died before the date of the document.
The material indicates that the deceased had begun cooperating with defrauded buyers, had demanded
return of money, and had stated an intention to give a written complaint shortly before his death. This is a
line of inquiry and not a finding.
The material suggests that the registered holding may not reflect actual beneficial ownership. Whether any
holding is benami requires examination of funding, possession, control, and intent under the applicable
law.
Repeated telephone contact, a requested meeting at an isolated farmhouse, and rapid outward movement of
collected consideration money may assist in prioritising investigation. They cannot, on their own, establish
presence at the scene, participation, motive, knowledge, or criminal responsibility.
Every extracted entity, financial relationship, graph link, movement record, or anomaly score must be
retained as a reviewable lead with source provenance and human validation before use.

I, Devkinandan Saini, state that I have worked in the office of Naresh Chand Meena, proprietor of Aravalli
Bhoomi Associates, for about four years. My duties are to receive buyers, write receipts in the receipt register,
keep the khasra file of every parcel, deposit cash and cheques in Marwar Kshetriya Bank at Chomu, and go to
the tehsil for copies of jamabandi and mutation entries.
From about October 2025 the office was dealing with the land of Khasra No. 412/6 and Khasra No. 418/2 of
village Nangal Bharda. Sahab told me that the parcels were being handled together with Kailash Narayan
Sharma and with Marudhar Estate Traders Pvt Ltd, and that the plotting brochure LAY-412-6-2026-04 had
been printed for buyers. I wrote receipts in registers RCP-ABA-2026-07 and RCP-ABA-2026-08.
Buyers paid by cheque, by bank transfer, and in some cases in cash. Sahab instructed me on several occasions
to transfer the collected money to the account of Marudhar Estate Traders Pvt Ltd, and I have myself written
the reference ACCT-8830471265 on the transfer slips at the bank counter. On two occasions I was told to send
money through the UPI identifier marudharestate@upi from the office phone.
In January 2026 I went to the patwar halka at Nangal Bharda for a copy of the jamabandi for Khasra No.
412/6. Sahab compared it with the papers given by Kailash Narayan Sharma and became upset, saying that the
khatedar name in the new mutation was not the same as in the old jamabandi and that mutation No.
1179/2025-26 had been sanctioned on a mukhtiyarnama which he did not believe was genuine. In February

2026 he obtained a photocopy of the power-of-attorney bearing reference DOC-CHM-2026-2184 and said that
the photograph fixed on it did not resemble the old khatedar and that the attesting witness name “Chhitar Mal”
was unknown to him. He kept that photocopy in the almirah in a green cloth file.
Kailash Narayan Sharma used to come to the office three or four times in a month, generally in a white
vehicle. In March and April 2026 there were loud arguments between him and Sahab in the inner room. On
one occasion in April I heard Sahab say that the land belonged to the heirs of the old khatedar, that the
company was only a paper name, and that the money should be returned to the buyers. I did not hear the whole
conversation.
On 14 May 2026 Om Prakash Yadav and Kamla Bai Jat came to the office and demanded their money back.
Om Prakash Yadav said that he had paid INR 47,00,000 and Kamla Bai Jat said that she had paid INR
18,50,000. Sahab told them to wait for one month and said that he would himself give an application to the
police about the papers. After they left he told me to keep the receipt registers, the khasra files, and the
photocopies in the almirah.
On 19 May 2026 at about 19:40 hours a call came on Sahab’s phone. He spoke in an angry voice and
afterwards showed me a message on the screen which said that he should come alone with the papers. Later I
identified that number as +91-88900-63354 from the office diary where Sahab had written it against the word
“Bhoora.”
On 21 May 2026 at about 19:55 hours Sahab received a call in the office. He spoke for two or three minutes
and then told me that he was going to the farmhouse near the Kaladera bypass cut for the final settlement and
that I should close the shop. He took the green cloth file with him and left on his motorcycle RJ-14-SM-2148.
That was the last time I saw him.
At about 21:30 hours I called Sahab on +91-94140-52286 because a buyer wanted to speak to him. The phone
rang but was not answered. I called again at about 21:50 hours and the phone was switched off. On 22 May
2026 in the morning I came to know about the incident from a neighbour of the family and I went to the
mortuary and identified the body.
I do not know who called Sahab on 21 May 2026, who prepared the mukhtiyarnama, who presented it for
registration, or in whose name the money finally went. I state this on the basis of my own work in the office
and what I personally saw, wrote, and heard. I have not removed, altered, or destroyed any office record, and I
am ready to produce the registers and files whenever required.

Financial Interpretation Note
The fictional records show buyer consideration credited to the agency account and transferred onward to a
counterparty account within hours, followed by further transfers to a second counterparty firm, a UPI
identifier, and a cash counter withdrawal shortly before and after the reported date of death. The narrations
describe the outward transfers as land share and facilitation payments, while the receipt register describes the
same amounts as consideration.
For an anomaly model, verified features could include transfer latency, repeat counterparty count, amount
concentration, incoming-to-outgoing ratio, cash-withdrawal share, transaction frequency, and network
centrality. These patterns are not proof that any transfer was improper, that any account was controlled by a
particular person, that any holding is benami, or that any financial entry is connected to the death. Certified
bank records, KYC data, beneficial-ownership information, incorporation and registration evidence,

Submission
1. FIR No. 519/2026 was registered on 05 September 2026 on the complaint of Deepak Chouhan concerning the
death of Aakash Chouhan, student-union General Secretary, following an altercation near the university canteen.
2. The case material refers to Complaint Ref. VCU-DISC-2026-0231 and Campus Security Incident Log Ref.
VCU-SEC-2026-0904, reflecting a documented rivalry between the Pragati Student Front and Unity Student
Alliance ahead of the scheduled union election.
3. Medico-legal referral has been made and a formal post-mortem and forensic board report is pending; the stated
cause-of-death category and incident window require confirmation through complete forensic documentation.
4. CDR data, vehicle movement records, an interrupted CCTV recording, and witness accounts indicate presence
of members of both student groups near the canteen during the relevant window; these are investigative leads
requiring corroboration and do not by themselves establish identity, intent, or criminal responsibility.
5. Further investigation is sought, subject to law, to identify all students involved in the altercation, obtain the
complete forensic report, examine the CCTV interruption, and determine whether an offence is established on
verified evidence.
